citations.narrative:
Some enclosures lacked barriers, thereby allowing public contact with animals. The facility representative conveyed an
attendant isn't always present in these areas to observe public interaction with these animals:
-In the west pastures, two reindeer were lying by the fence where the public could touch them. In the adjacent pasture,
members of the public are allowed to feed goats facility-provided feed and pet them through the fence.
-An enclosure housing a young wolf lacked a barrier to prevent the ability to reach inside the enclosure for the possibility
of contact. The lack of a barrier doesn't prevent possible contact if the wolf goes to the front of the enclosure.
The lack of a public barrier that allows contact with animals such as reindeer, goats and a young wolf does not minimize
risk of harm to the animals or to the public. Ensure that an adequate barrier and/or distance between the animals and
general viewing public so as to assure the safety of animals and the public
***Correct by 7/10/2026.

Two Call ducks had a space for wading that wasn't large enough to bathe/swim. Lack of a sufficient swimming area
doesn't provide for their normal behaviors. Ensure that these ducks are provided with an aquatic space that has sufficient
surface area and depth to allow each bird to make normal postural and social adjustments, such as immersion, bathing,
swimming, and foraging, with adequate freedom of movement.
***Correct by 7/13/2026.
This inspection and exit interview were conducted with a facility representative.
Additional Inspectors:
Lynne White-Shim, Supervisory Animal Care Specialist n
